final_answer:
DEVIATION REPORT: DRAFT CREDIT AGREEMENT (Caldwell Strauss draft 4/18/25, "CA") v. EXECUTED TERM SHEET (3/14/25, "TS") - $285M Facilities, Cascade Environmental Solutions / Ridgeline National Bank. Borrower-side (Hargrove) review.

1. BOTTOM LINE
Lender's counsel's 4/18 transmittal calls the changes "administrative and mechanical." They are not. I count 6 critical, 14 high and roughly 15 moderate deviations, most adverse to Borrower. Several omit TS protections (equity cure, SunGard, Guarantor/collateral carve-outs) and several add new lender rights (key-man Change of Control, financial-covenant tightening). TS Sec. 16 says the definitive CA controls over the TS, and the TS is non-binding except confidentiality, exclusivity, expenses and governing law. Fix every item in the draft. The email's "credit committee approval ... on terms not materially less favorable to the Lenders than those reflected in this draft" is a negotiating anchor; reject it in writing. Timing: comments requested ~May 2, 2025 (10 business days); closing 5/30/25; TS exclusivity ends 5/30; TS Outside Date 6/30/25, so Borrower's leverage is time-limited. Do not share the draft beyond the deal team without Agent consent (email confidentiality note).

2. CRITICAL DEVIATIONS (negotiate as must-haves)
C1 Equity cure deleted. TS 11.4 gives Sponsor cure rights (15 BD; 2 per four quarters, 4 life; EBITDA cure). CA has none: 8.01(b) makes 7.11 breaches immediate, no-cure Events of Default. Fix: insert TS 11.4 verbatim as new 7.11(d), amend 8.01(b). Risk: critical.
C2 Change of Control. CA 1.01 raises threshold from 50% (TS 12(a)) to 50.1% of Holdings voting power, drops "co-investors and related funds," and adds clause (d): David Whitmore ceasing to be "actively involved" in Sponsor management. TS says CoC "is limited to the ownership threshold and structural control provisions." Clause (d) is an uncontrolled key-man Event of Default (8.01(j)) and contradicts TS. Also CA 4.13(b) represents Fund holds not less than 50.1%. Fix: delete (d); restore 50% and affiliate/co-investor language; narrow (c) to acceleration-triggering events (CA's narrower (c) is an improvement; keep it).
C3 No SunGard/certain-funds conditionality. TS 6(n) requires limited conditionality (Specified Representations/Defaults). CA 3.01(e) requires all reps true and no Default at closing; 3.01(q) uses the CA's own MAE rather than the Acquisition Agreement MAE (TS 6(e)); 3.01(r) adds a no-litigation condition; 3.01(f) demands three years of audits (TS: FY2024 only); 3.01(b) adds Ohio/Delaware local-counsel opinions; 3.01(g) is "consistent with those described to" Agent (TS 6(b): no materially adverse modifications). "Specified Representations" is never defined. Fix: add SunGard definitions and limit 3.01(e); conform MAE to the SPA; delete 3.01(r), extra audit years, extra opinions.
C4 Financial-definition tightening (covenant squeeze). (a) Unrestricted Cash netting cap $10M (CA 1.01, 7.11(a)) v. $15M (TS 11.1), and the definition adds "unencumbered," Control-Agreement-only, no-foreign-cash limits; (b) Adjusted EBITDA drops TS add-backs for non-recurring and cash restructuring charges (CA adds back only non-cash items), caps Acquisition transaction costs at 12 months, and nets realized savings against the 20% synergy add-back; (c) Funded Debt references the broad "Indebtedness" definition (guarantees, net swaps, deferred purchase price) rather than TS borrowed-money debt; (d) Capex (7.10) counts financed capex. Illustration: TS shows 4.01x at close using $185M debt and $14M cash. But TS Sources apply that $14M cash to uses, and TS Total Funded Debt includes capital leases (CA Sch. 7.02: $2.1M). On CA definitions, closing leverage is (185+2.1-10)/42.6 = 4.16x, or 4.39x if closing cash is nil, leaving roughly 7.6-12.4% EBITDA cushion to the 4.75x covenant. Fix: restore $15M cap, TS EBITDA add-backs, TS Funded Debt/Unrestricted Cash definitions; run a covenant model before responding.
C5 DDTL cut. Availability Period 12 months/May 30, 2026 (CA 1.01, 2.03(d), 3.02(d)) v. 18 months/Nov 30, 2026 (TS 3.3); draws limited to 3 at $10M minimum (CA 2.03(b)) v. unlimited draws at $5M minimum. Permitted Acquisition (CA 1.01) also tightened: single-deal cap $20M v. $25M (TS 9.5(a)); notice 15 BD v. 10 BD; new QoE report above $10M; earn-outs counted. Structural problem inherited from TS: acquisitions need pro forma leverage of not more than 4.00x, yet closing leverage is about 4.2-4.4x, so the DDTL may be unusable in the shortened window. Fix: restore TS terms; request 4.50x (or covenant-level) acquisition test stepping down.
C6 Collateral/Guarantor scope. TS Sec. 5 excludes immaterial subs (<5% assets), foreign subs, unrestricted subs, SPEs; limits foreign pledges to 65% voting; real property only above $2.5M FMV. CA has no exclusions: every Subsidiary must guarantee (Sch. 4.13 note; 5.11), "all assets" are Collateral, mortgages "material" real property. Fix: add Excluded Subsidiary/Excluded Assets definitions per TS (and, for a remediation company, permits/licenses non-assignable by law).

3. HIGH-PRIORITY DEVIATIONS
H1 SOFR floor 1.00% (CA 1.01 "SOFR," 2.08(a), 1.06(b)) v. 0.75% (TS 4.1). About $462,500/yr on $185M when floor binds. Also CA defines "SOFR" as overnight SOFR, not Term SOFR (TS 4.1), while Interest Periods are 1/3/6-month; no CME Term SOFR definition or stated 0% spread adjustment. Fix: 0.75%; define Term SOFR.
H2 Revolver grid: CA drops Level 3 (<3.00x: S+3.25%) (2.08(a); Ex. D) - up to 25 bps (about $125K/yr if fully drawn); changes become effective 5th BD after certificate v. 1st BD (TS 4.2). Restore three levels and 1st BD.
H3 Capex covenant 7.10 $10.5M v. $12M (TS 9.4); carryforward (25%, up to $3M, one year) deleted; effective capacity falls 12.5%, 30% against TS maximum. Restore (CA's lack of partial-year proration helps 2025; keep).
H4 Restricted Payments 7.06: management fee $1.0M v. $1.5M (TS 9.3(c)) and bar on payment during any Default (TS: subordination/deferral only on Event of Default; require accrual and catch-up); tax distributions subject to 7.06(e) no-Default bar although TS 9.3(b) allows them "at all times"; no general dividend basket (TS 9.3(a): permitted if no EoD and pro forma covenant compliance); employee repurchases capped $500K (TS "to be agreed").
H5 Annual audited financials due 90 days (5.01(a)) v. 120 days (TS 8(a)); going-concern qualification prohibited (TS allows maturity-driven qualification). Budget required monthly v. quarterly (5.01(d)). Since the ECF payment is keyed to delivery, an early deadline also accelerates sweeps. Restore 120 days.
H6 Events of Default (8.01) v. TS Sec. 12: interest/fee grace 3 BD v. 5 BD; judgment default 30 days v. 60; cross-default triggers on mere right to accelerate, counts undrawn commitments, no acceleration/maturity requirement (TS 12(f)); representation default "in any respect" for materiality-qualified reps; insolvency reaches any Loan Party (TS: Borrower, Guarantors, material subs); new Environmental EoD (8.01(k)) (TS has an MAE EoD, which CA omits - take the trade, but limit (k) to MAE-level, final judgments). Restore TS.
H7 Default interest (2.08(b)): applies to all Obligations incl. fees, from date of EoD, v. TS 4.1 overdue amounts. Narrow to overdue amounts.
H8 Mandatory prepayments (2.05(b)) v. TS Sec. 10: ECF definition drops TS clause (g) deduction for cash Permitted Acquisition consideration and adds only $3M life-of-deal restructuring deduction; omits $2.0M gross minimum threshold and dollar-for-dollar voluntary-prepayment credit (TS 10.1); ECF payment applied pro rata TLA/DDTL (TS: TLA first). Insurance reinvestment 180 days v. 270 (TS 10.4); asset-sale reinvestment drops 180-day committed-reinvestment extension (TS 10.2) and requires notice within 10 BD. (Business interruption exclusion and "other assets" reinvestment are Borrower-favorable; keep.) Note ECF is 50% at 4.00x+, likely triggered for FY2025.
H9 Leverage-covenant step-downs (7.11(a)): CA schedule is later by one to two quarters than TS 11.1/Ex. B (e.g., 4.75x through 6/30/26 v. 3/31/26; 4.00x from 3/31/28 v. 12/31/27). Borrower-favorable; accept silently, but see C4. Test start 9/30/25 matches TS.
H10 Incremental Facility (2.14), $40M, not in TS. Mixed: lender-discretionary, MFN (50 bps incl. floors, 6-month sunset) only; 2.14(d) bypasses TS 14(d) unanimous-consent for commitment increases, while 10.01(a) omits TS 14(d)-(e) (increases; lien subordination). Email calls it "borrower-friendly"; it mainly protects existing Lenders. Confirm intent; seek ratio-based capacity.
H11 Fee Letter. CA defines it as dated March 28, 2025 among Borrower, Holdings and Ridgeline; TS Sec. 17 says executed March 14 among Borrower, Sponsor and Agent. Obtain and compare; CA makes it a Loan Document (cross-default exposure).
H12 Assignments (10.06): no Disqualified Institution list (TS 13(e)); add. Borrower consent also required for Lender/affiliate/Approved Fund assignments (Borrower-favorable v. TS 13(d)).
H13 Indemnity/expenses (10.04): TS 15 limits to one primary counsel plus one local per jurisdiction; CA covers "any counsel"; adds claims brought by Borrower and "Environmental Liability related in any way to" Borrower (TS: presence/release on owned, leased, operated property); drops "bad faith" carve-out; adds syndication expenses. Restore TS.
H14 Post-closing (5.12/Sch. 5.12): TS 8(p) 90 days; CA items 30/60/90/120 days, with miss an Event of Default. Inconsistency: 3.01(j)-(l) require insurance and UCC-1 evidence at closing, yet Sch. 5.12 items 4-5 defer them 30 days. Align to 90 days/extension by Agent.

4. MODERATE / CLEAN-UP
- Amortization (2.06): payments start 9/30/25; schedule has 19 installments (11 in years 3-5) v. 20 (12) under TS 3.1/Ex. A: $74.0M v. $78.625M, balloon $111.0M v. $106.375M. Favorable on cash, but confirm. DDTL amortization (2.07) tied to "same schedule," ambiguous v. TS 3.3 (per-draw years); clarify.
- Liens basket $2M general; debt: extra $1M general basket; asset-sale "other" $500K - TS silent; request larger.
- Fiscal-year change consent: Agent v. Required Lenders (TS 9.7(d)); Borrower-favorable.
- Affirmative covenants: CA adds mandatory environmental/business-interruption insurance (5.07), 5-BD notices, $1M litigation notice, and pension underfunding rep $5M (4.12(b)); but omits TS "enhanced" environmental reporting.
- NY GOL 5-1401 reference and SDNY-first jurisdiction (TS 16) omitted; low risk.
- Defaulting Lender 2.15 cross-refers to replacement under 2.19 (increased-cost section) - mis-reference.
- Undefined terms: Subordinated Indebtedness, Investment, Eligible Assignee, Approved Fund, Change in Law, Credit Extension, Total Credit Exposures, Revolving Credit Exposure, SOFR/Base Rate Loan, Benchmark Replacement Date, Bail-In Action, Capital Lease Obligations, LC Exposure. Article VI is "reserved" though the email places information covenants there (they sit in 5.01-5.02).
- Closing Date, Availability Period and maturity are hard-coded dates; define relative to actual closing in case of slippage toward the 6/30 Outside Date.
- Signature/notice details: Holdings signatory "Thomas Elridge, VP" (TS: David Whitmore); Agent title "Managing Director" (TS: SVP); Mr. Delvecchio signs for Ridgeline as Lender; notice emails (rthayer@hpllaw.com, kfulton@, jdelvecchio@, pgranville@csmlaw.com) differ from email-header domains (hargrovepl.com, ridgelinenational.com, caldwellstrauss.com). Correct.
- Conforming items (no deviation): facility amounts, $3.2M LCs, $10M LC sublimit, margins (S+3.75%), commitment fee grid, ticking fee, maturity 5/30/30, ECF percentages, 1/3/6 month periods, 2% default margin, NY law, jury waiver, 15% rollover, $55M/$30M equity, covenant levels FCCR 1.20x and liquidity $10M. Note email lists 1/3/6-month periods as an "addition"; they are already in TS 4.1.

5. TERM SHEET RED FLAGS (resolve with Sponsor before signing reps)
- Sources and Uses: sources total $384.0M only by counting the undrawn $50M Revolver and $50M DDTL; funded sources are $284M, leaving a $100M gap v. $384M uses. CA 3.01(i) and 4.13(b) bake in the equity numbers.
- Equity: $55M Fund + $30M rollover implies rollover about 35%, not 15% (TS Sec. 1-2; CA 4.13(b) repeats "approximately 15%"). A wrong rep is an Event of Default (8.01(d), no cure).
- Closing leverage double counts cash and omits capital leases (see C4). Flag to Sponsor/financial advisor.
- FCCR stress: at illustrative 8% all-in rate, interest is about $14.8M plus $9.25M year-one amortization (about $24M); 1.20x needs about $29M of EBITDA less capex/taxes, i.e., capex plus cash taxes under about $13.7M, against a $10.5M capex cap. Tight; model it (assumption, not from documents).

6. EMAIL v. DRAFT (mischaracterizations)
"Hardwired" benchmark replacement: 1.06 is amendment-based. "Administrative" definitions: MAE (adds Loan-Document performance and Lender-rights prongs, no carve-outs, v. TS 12 carve-outs "consistent with market practice"), CoC and covenant definitions are substantive. Basket/timing "calibrated to credit committee" confirm TS departures (capex, RP, prepayments). "Fully built out" ECF omits TS protections. MAE: add customary carve-outs and align with SPA.

7. NEXT STEPS
1) Circulate this report to Sponsor and Mr. Jennings; confirm business priorities (C1-C6 first). 2) Respond by May 2 with markup restoring TS; state in cover note that TS economics are not reopened and the credit committee condition is rejected. 3) Request Fee Letter, SPA, Sch. 2.04, closing checklist. 4) Reconcile Sources/Uses and equity percentages. 5) Run covenant model (leverage, FCCR, liquidity, capex). 6) Calendar: exclusivity expires 5/30; Outside Date 6/30.
